context:
Take the classification rule written by [mcp-option-contract-matrix-enforcement] w1 and apply it. Two shapes, both already validated by the ClickHouse item; prefer (a) unless remote Velox over MCP is a real demand:
  (a) Remove `deployment` from MCP_PLATFORM_OPTION_ALLOWLIST['velox']. Local is the only Velox deployment MCP can fully describe -- endpoint, gluten_jar_path and the rest are not admissible -- so a caller asking for `remote` is asking for a run this boundary cannot configure. Record the removal in the docs/reference/mcp.md omission ledger with a ratified tier, per the one-engine ADR; an unledgered omission is itself a defect.
  (b) If remote Velox must stay reachable, mirror BENCHBOX_MCP_CLICKHOUSE_PROFILES: a server-owned velox endpoint registry, accept only a profile name, resolve in the adapter-facing translation at EXECUTION time so durable replays re-resolve, and reject deployment='remote' without a profile.
Either way, tests/unit/mcp/test_schemas.py:272 currently asserts `remote` is accepted -- that assertion encodes the assumption and must change with the fix.
description:
The ClickHouse remediation (#1510) established that a connection-class platform option must NAME a server-owned destination, never DESCRIBE one. `velox.deployment` is classified security_class='connection' in MCP_PLATFORM_OPTION_CONTRACT but was never brought under that rule, so an authenticated MCP caller can still steer the server at a listener the operator never approved.

Reproduced on develop 4836e3988d:
  validate_platform_options('velox', {'deployment': 'remote'})  -> {'deployment': 'remote'}  (accepted)
  _prepare_adapter_platform_options('velox', ...)               -> {'deployment': 'remote'}  (unchanged)
  VeloxAdapter.from_config(...).endpoint                        -> 'sc://localhost:50051'

benchbox/platforms/velox.py:153 defaults the Spark-Connect endpoint to sc://localhost:50051 when the caller supplies none, and MCP does not allow `endpoint`, so `remote` always resolves to that fixed host-local target. velox.py:370 then calls SparkSession.builder.remote(endpoint); :389-393 probes reachability and raises an error whose text contains the endpoint. A caller who cannot choose a port still learns whether a Spark-Connect server is listening on localhost:50051, and can cause a connection attempt to it.

Narrower than the ClickHouse finding (one fixed port, not caller-chosen), and on a remote deployment the operator's allowed_platforms policy must already include velox for it to be reachable -- hence high, not critical. But it is the same defect class the batch was convened to close, left open in the platform whose item (#1520) touched this exact option: #1520 closed only the enumeration half (deployment='docker' now fails closed) and left `remote` admissible.

TIMING. benchbox/mcp/tools/benchmark.py is scheduled for rewrite by one-engine-mcp-run-service-adoption, whose rung 1 requires _prepare_adapter_platform_options to be deleted. This item is small and must land BEFORE that rewrite, or the fix has to be re-authored against a moved execution path.

Identified 2026-08-04 during the adversarial review of the mcp-v2-platform-options batch.

SUPERSEDES `mcp-velox-remote-destination-boundary`, which was dropped minutes after creation on 2026-08-04 to attach anti-patterns, sequenced work units, prior art and dependency edges. `drop` is a soft state change rather than a delete, so the original id could not be reused; the dropped item carries the reason and links back here.

anti_patterns.dont: add `endpoint` to the MCP allow-list so that `remote` becomes fully describable
anti_patterns.instead: if remote must work, callers name a server-owned profile and never describe one
anti_patterns.why: that is exactly the caller-supplied destination the ClickHouse item removed; it converts a one-port probe into arbitrary host and port selection

anti_patterns.dont: fix this by suppressing the endpoint from the _ensure_server_ready error text
anti_patterns.instead: stop the request at admission, or bind it to a server-owned destination
anti_patterns.why: the connection ATTEMPT is the boundary crossing, not just its error message -- redacting the message leaves the server still dialling a listener the operator never approved, and leaves timing as an oracle

anti_patterns.dont: keep tests/unit/mcp/test_schemas.py:272 asserting that deployment='remote' is accepted
anti_patterns.instead: replace it with the post-fix contract, and add a case proving MCP cannot produce an adapter aimed at an unapproved endpoint
anti_patterns.why: that assertion is what pinned the assumption in the first place; leaving it forces the fix to route around its own regression test

anti_patterns.dont: land this after one-engine-mcp-run-service-adoption rewrites benchbox/mcp/tools/benchmark.py
anti_patterns.instead: land this first; it is a small, self-contained admission change
anti_patterns.why: the adoption deletes _prepare_adapter_platform_options, so a fix authored against it would have to be rewritten and re-reviewed against a moved execution path

preserves.behavior: CLI and direct-constructor use of VeloxAdapter(deployment='remote', endpoint=...) keeps working unchanged: this is an MCP admission boundary, not an adapter capability change
The ClickHouse profile boundary is untouched: no change to resolve_clickhouse_connection_profile timing or to what a durable job persists
deployment='docker' keeps failing closed with the existing explanatory hint added by #1520

prior_art.concept: resolve_clickhouse_connection_profile and _validate_clickhouse_options (#1510) are the server-owned destination pattern; extend that pattern if shape (b) is chosen rather than inventing a second registry format
the 'Server-owned ClickHouse connection profiles' section states the rule; generalize its wording to all connection-class options instead of appending a parallel Velox section
the omission ledger with ratified tiers, mandated by the one-engine ADR; shape (a) must add a tier-tagged row because an unledgered omission is itself a defect
test_clickhouse_profile_withdrawn_by_the_operator_fails_closed is the withdrawal-test shape to copy if shape (b) is chosen
